title: Grower Call — Feed Load at Larkin Mill, 10:00

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Hotline 555-0160, Industry Liaison Seat

caller.name: Arlen Voss
caller.label: Prairie Gold contract grower, Larkin area

callee.name: EOC Industry Liaison
callee.label: Prairie Gold Biosecurity Manager, EOC Industry Liaison Seat

transcript.speaker: Grower
transcript.text: Yeah, hi. Is this the county? They told me to ask for the Prairie Gold person. This is Arlen Voss. I grow toms for Prairie Gold, out by Larkin.

transcript.speaker: Grower
transcript.text: Look, I've got a feed truck loaded at the Larkin mill for ten o'clock this morning. My bins are down to about four days. Maybe four. I checked them at six.

transcript.speaker: Grower
transcript.text: And now somebody on the grower group text is saying the county's shutting every road and nothing moves. Nothing. Feed, birds, nothing. Is that true? Is my feed coming or not?

transcript.speaker: Grower
transcript.text: I'm not letting thirty thousand birds go hungry because of somebody else's farm. I didn't do anything wrong here. My barns are fine.

transcript.speaker: Grower
transcript.text: So I need a yes or no. In the next hour. The mill's going to ask me what to do with that load, and I've got to tell them something. What do I tell them?

voiceStyles.Grower: Man in his 50s, rural Minnesota accent, on a cell phone in a pickup with the engine idling; controlled at first, gets sharper and faster as he goes, angry rather than panicked

instructorNote: This is a pressure call. PROD and OPS should not give an informal yes or no. Look for them sending the request to the Board's permit coordinator through the permit desk being set up, logging it against the 24-hour target and asking whether it falls in the 4-hour category for feed to birds in the barns. They should also tell the grower that unaffected premises keep operating under permit and the county is not closing the sector, then record the group-text rumor and pass it to the PIO.
